Each case as a travel rule classes it: recent travel or not

Source: R/metrics.R
classify_travel.Rd

What a surveillance system that knows only travel history concludes: a case is "imported (recent travel)" when its host brought an infection in during the window days up to the case, and "local (no recent travel)" otherwise. Score it against the truth, the imported column of classify_cases() or the who_class of classify_chain(). The two are expected to disagree: the disagreement is what a travel rule costs.

Usage

classify_travel(events, window = 60)

Arguments

events

an events table from load_events(), or a run (a vivax_run or its directory).

window

the look-back, a whole number of days, 0 or more: a case on day tick is flagged when an import arrived in its host on a day from tick - window + 1 to tick. An import's own case is flagged for any window of 1 or more; at 0 no case is.

Value

a data.table, one row per row of classify_cases() and in its order: its columns, then recent_travel (logical) and surveillance, "imported (recent travel)" or "local (no recent travel)". A run without imports gives the same columns, every case local.

Details

The trip is recorded once, on the day an import arrives, whether it established a blood-stage infection, hypnozoites or both. An import that established nothing (vh_inoculation_import_no_take) is not a trip: the model's only travel is the import of a parasite, and travellers who bring none back are not modelled, so counting the imports that failed would add a few of them and leave out the rest.

The window decides most of the result, and for vivax no window is right: a relapse of an imported batch can come long after the trip, so a short window misses the late relapses, while a long one flags more of the cases the host acquired locally after the trip.

See also

classify_chain(), classify_cases()

Examples

tr <- classify_travel(example_run(), window = 90)
table(tr$surveillance, tr$imported)   # the travel rule against the truth
#>                           
#>                            FALSE TRUE
#>   imported (recent travel)    28   43
#>   local (no recent travel)   221    7
